subject: Alternative to saving mcmc samples as R matrix

messages.subject: Alternative to saving mcmc samples as R matrix
parts:
Hi All,

I tried searching the group posts but couldn't find what I'm looking for. I have a model that seems to run fine and the MCMC will finish, but when I try pulling the samples into R I run into memory problems (there are 1000*1300ish nodes and a correspondingly large samples matrix). Is there an alternative way to save the samples to disk so that I can try other large matrix approaches (hdf5 or something)?

C

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Alternative to saving mcmc samples as R matrix
parts:
Hi Chris,

Let's say your compiled mcmc is called cmcmc.

If by pulling the samples into R, you mean the common step of "as.matrix(cmcmc$mvSamples)", yes, you can take more fine-grained control over that.  If instead you are using either nimbleMCMC or creating cmcmc and then using runMCMC(cmcmc,...), you will instead need to call cmcmc$run(...) yourself so you can take control of retrieving the samples.

The object cmcmc$mvSamples is what we call a compiled modelValues object.  Please check out Chapter 14 of the User Manual to see how you can access its contents in more or less natural R style, like cmcmc$mvSamples[["beta"]].  There is also concise information in help(modelValuesBaseClass), as directed from help(modelValues).

You might also find the monitors2 and thin2 system helpful, if you can get by with smaller samples (more thinning) for some of your variables.

Responses will be slow for a few days.

-Perry
